Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 74, verse 1:

(p-361) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah al-Muddaththir (The Cloaked One).

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who are wrapped up﴾ ﴿arise and warn﴾

Al-Indhar (warning, admonition) is informing with intimidation (takhwif). It is therefore more specific than mere informing (al-i'lam), and it is transitive to two objects: the one warned (al-mundhir), in the form of the object, and that concerning which one is warned (al-mundhar bihi). Neither of them is mentioned here.

As for the one warned, other verses have made clear that it may be the disbelievers, as in His saying: ﴿and you warn thereby a stubborn people﴾ [Maryam: 97], intimidating them.

It may also be the believers, since they are the ones who benefit from it, as in His saying: ﴿You can only warn one who follows the Reminder and fears the Most Merciful in the unseen﴾ [Ya-Sin: 11].

It may also be for all, that is, for mankind in general, as in His saying exalted is He: ﴿Is it a wonder for the people that We revealed to a man from among them: warn the people and give good tidings to those who believe﴾ [Yunus: 2].

As for that concerning which one is warned, it is what will occur on the Day of Resurrection.

Ibn Jarir has specified both matters here, saying: "Warn of the punishment of Allah your people who associated others with Allah and worshipped other than Him."

The Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, has already given a detailed explanation of this under His saying: ﴿so that you may warn thereby, and as a reminder for the believers﴾ [al-A'raf: 2], in Surah al-A'raf.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 74, verse 4:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And your garments, purify﴾

The exegetes have differed over the intended meaning of each of the two words: "garments" (al-thiyab) and "purify" (fa-tahhir). Do both words denote their literal meanings, such that what is intended is the purification of the garment from impurities (najasat)? Or do they denote figuratively (kinayah)? And by "garment" is meant the body, and "purification" is from immaterial matters, such as sins, transgressions and the like? Or is it a mixture of the literal and the figurative? Ibn Jarir and others have mentioned about five opinions:

(p-362) The first: from Ibn 'Abbas, 'Ikrimah and al-Dahhak, that its meaning is: do not wear your garments for disobedience, nor for treachery. He cited the verse of Ghaylan:

"And by the praise of God, I have not worn the garment of a wicked person, nor do I veil myself with treachery."

And the saying of another:

"When a man's honour is not defiled by baseness, every garment he wears is beautiful."

Thus he used both words in the figurative sense. It may be supported by His saying: ﴿And We removed from you your burden﴾ [al-Sharh: 2].

It is also reported from Ibn 'Abbas: do not wear your garments from unlawful earnings. Thus he used "garments" in the literal sense and "purification" in the figurative sense.

From Mujahid: "Set right your deeds, and your deeds, then set them right," so he used both together in the figurative sense of righteous deeds.

From Muhammad ibn Sirin and Ibn Zayd: both in their literal senses, that is, purify your garments from impurity.

Then he said: what Ibn Sirin and Ibn Zayd said is more apparent in this matter.

The saying of Ibn 'Abbas and 'Ikrimah is a view upon which most of the early generation (al-salaf) agree. And God knows best His intent.

Others said: "your garments" are your wives, as in His saying ﴿They are a garment for you﴾ [al-Baqarah: 187]; so command them to purify themselves, and choose for them women who are pure and good.

These are the sayings of the exegetes, and Ibn Jarir's choice among them; and what occurs in the context supports Ibn Jarir's choice, namely, taking both words in their literal senses.

The preference for Ibn Sirin's view, that what is meant is the purification of the garment from impurity, is supported by the indication within the verse, for it includes two matters: the first is the purification of the garment, and the second is abandoning the rijz.

Among the meanings of rijz is sins. So taking the purification of the garment in its literal sense, and the rijz in its literal sense with a new meaning, is preferable.

(p-363) This verse, in both its parts, has a counterpart in both its parts stated more clearly in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And He sends down upon you water from the sky to purify you thereby and remove from you the rijz of Satan﴾ [al-Anfal: 11]. And God, exalted is He, knows best.

Al-Shafi'i made this verse a proof for purity as a condition for prayer.

**Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on Surah 74, verses 8–10:**

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿When the trumpet is sounded,﴾ ﴿that will be a difficult day,﴾ ﴿not easy for the disbelievers.﴾

*Al-Naqur* (the trumpet) is *al-Sur*, and the root of *al-naqur* is *al-sawt* (the sound). As for His words, ﴿a difficult day﴾ and ﴿not easy for the disbelievers﴾:

It has been said: it is difficult, and not easy, for the disbelievers.

Al-Zamakhshari said: "Indeed, ﴿not easy﴾ would have sufficed in place of ﴿difficult day﴾, but He says it to make clear to them that its difficulty is not expected to be eased, like the difficulty of this world, and that there is in it an added threat to the disbelievers."

It is also a kind of good news for the believers, because it is easy for them. Perhaps the two meanings are independent. And the words of Allah the Exalted, ﴿a difficult day﴾, are an independent statement describing this day and explaining to all its extreme terror, as He described it in His words: ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord. Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a tremendous thing. On the day you see it, every nursing mother will forget what she nursed, and every pregnant one will lay down her load, and you will see people as intoxicated, but they will not be intoxicated; rather, the punishment of Allah will be severe﴾ [al-Ḥajj: 1–2], and like His words: ﴿On the Day a man will flee from his brother, and his mother and his father﴾ [ʿAbasa: 34–35], and the like of that.

Then Allah the Exalted made clear that this difficult day is ﴿not easy for the disbelievers﴾, as He said about them: ﴿How, then, will you guard yourselves, if you disbelieve, against a Day that will turn children white-haired? The sky will be split by it﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 17–18]. Whereas for the believers it will be easy, although it is difficult in itself because of the severity of its terror, but Allah makes it easy for the believers. Allah also clarified this image alongside its counterpart in His words in Surah "al-Naml":

﴿And the Day the trumpet is blown, whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will be terrified, except whom Allah wills; and all will come to Him in humility.﴾ ﴿And you see the mountains, thinking them rigid, while they pass like the passing of clouds…﴾ up to His words: ﴿Whoever brings a good deed will have better than it, and they will be safe from the terror of that Day. And whoever brings an evil deed, their faces will be thrown into the Fire. Are you recompensed except for what you used to do?﴾ [al-Naml: 87–90].

[p. 364] So the terror resulting from the blast on the Day the trumpet is blown is general to all who are in the heavens and all who are on the earth, but Allah excepted whom He willed. Then Allah clarified who these exceptions are and who remains in terror: He made clear the secure, who are those who brought the good deed, and the others, who are those who brought the evil deed.

**Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 74, verse 30:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Over it are nineteen.﴾ ﴿We have made none but angels the guardians of the Fire, and We have not made their number except as a trial for those who disbelieve, so that those who were given the Scripture may be certain, and those who believe may increase in faith, and those who were given the Scripture and the believers may not doubt, and so that those in whose hearts is disease and the disbelievers may say, "What did Allah intend by this as an example?" Thus Allah leaves astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills. And none knows the soldiers of your Lord except Him. And it is nothing but a reminder to mankind.﴾

Concerning His saying, ﴿We have not made their number except as a trial (fitnah, "test, ordeal") for those who disbelieve﴾, al-Qurtubi mentioned two meanings of fitnah here:

The first: burning, as in His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who put to trial the believing men and believing women...﴾ [Al-Buruj: 10].

The second: testing. The Shaykh has previously stated many times in his book and his lessons that the original meaning of fitnah is examination. You say: "I tested the gold" when you put it into the fire so that you may know its counterfeit from its pure part.

However, the context indicates the second meaning, which is testing and trial, by His saying: ﴿and so that those in whose hearts is disease and the disbelievers may say, "What did Allah intend by this as an example?"﴾

And His saying: ﴿And none knows the soldiers of your Lord except Him﴾, meaning their number. If the intended meaning were burning and the threat of the Fire, there would be no room for the questioning of those in whose hearts is disease and of the disbelievers concerning this example, nor would it be appropriate to make it an example, nor would the speech about the number of the soldiers of your Lord have any relevance. This noble verse contains several important issues.

The first: the making of the mentioned example, that is, the making of this specified number a trial, so that it provokes questioning or is met with submission. Those who find it implausible asked questions, while the believers submitted and acquiesced, as He, the Exalted, mentioned in His explicit statement: ﴿Indeed, Allah is not ashamed to present an example, [even] of a mosquito or what is smaller than it. As for those who believe, they know that it is the truth from their Lord; but as for those who disbelieve, they say, "What did Allah intend by this as an example?"﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 26].

Then He, the Exalted, explained the purpose of that in accordance with what came in the verse here: ﴿By it He misleads many and by it He guides many, and He misleads thereby none but the defiantly disobedient﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 26]. (p-365) This verse from Surat al-Baqarah fully clarifies the verse of al-Muddaththir.

The second issue: His saying, ﴿so that those who were given the Scripture may be certain﴾, indicates that this agrees with what is in their Torah. This is among the things that bear witness for their people to the truthfulness of what the Prophet ﷺ brings, and to what he claimed concerning their belief and affirmation.

Al-Qurtubi mentioned a hadith on this and considered it strange, but the text bears witness to it.

The third issue: whenever a believer receives a command from Allah and affirms it, even if he does not know its reality, being content that it is from Allah, his affirmation increases his faith. This is the issue of the increase of faith through obedience and affirmation.

The fourth issue: an explanation that it is obligatory for the believer to hasten to affirmation and submission, even if he does not know the wisdom, secret, or purpose, on the basis that the report is from Allah, the Exalted. He is the most knowing of what He has related.

Concerning this issue there arises the debate over the wisdom of legislation. This is a broad matter. But what is important for us here, while we are in an age of materialism, the advance of inventions, and the appearance of many question marks regarding many verses of rulings, is that we wish to say:

Every ruling that is authentically established from the Wise Lawgiver, whether in the Book or the Sunnah, must be accepted and submitted to, whether or not we know its wisdom, because our knowledge is limited, our understanding is restricted, and the All-Knowing, the All-Wise, the Kind, the Merciful, glory be to Him, does not impose on His servants except what contains wisdom.

In summary, rulings with respect to their wisdom may be confined to three categories:

The first category: a ruling whose wisdom is made manifest by a text, as in the obligation of prayer, where it came: ﴿Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing﴾ [Al-Ankabut: 45]. This is a sublime wisdom. And concerning zakah it came that it: ﴿purifies them and causes them to grow﴾ [At-Tawbah: 103].

Concerning fasting it came: ﴿so that you may become righteous﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 183].

Concerning hajj it came: ﴿that they may witness benefits for themselves﴾ [Al-Hajj: 28]. Although these are acts of worship to Allah, their wisdom has clearly appeared.

Concerning the prohibited matters, as the scholars have said regarding the six essential necessities: the preservation of religion, intellect, life, honor, lineage, and property, for the maintenance of life, the abundance of security, and the protection of society. Boundaries (hudud) have been set within them for their preservation, and so on.

The second category: a ruling whose wisdom has not appeared with this clarity, but which is not devoid of wisdom, such as circumambulation (tawaf), running between Safa and Marwa (sa'y), bowing (ruku'), prostration (sujud), ablution (wudu'), dry ablution (tayammum), ritual bathing (ghusl), and the like.

The third category: a ruling that is first a trial and examination, and then has wisdom, such as the changing of the qiblah, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We did not make the qiblah which you used to face except that We might make evident who would follow the Messenger from who would turn back on his heels﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 143].

In the turning away from it there is wisdom, as in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿so that people will have no argument against you﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 150].

The Muslim, in both states, whether the wisdom became apparent to him or did not, is obligated to comply and submit, as «Umar said when he kissed the Black Stone: "I know that you are a stone that neither harms nor benefits. Had I not seen the Messenger of Allah ﷺ kissing you, I would not have kissed you."»

So he kissed it, complying and following, setting aside what had come from: that 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, said to him: "Yes, O Commander of the Faithful, it does harm and it does benefit. On the Day of Resurrection it will come with a tongue and two eyes, and will bear witness for whoever kissed it." This was because 'Umar approached it to kiss it before 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, informed him.

Matters may also be uncovered to reveal a wisdom we do not know, as in the story of al-Khidr with Musa, peace be upon them both, when he tore the ship, killed the boy, and rebuilt the wall. All of these were actions for which Musa, peace be upon him, did not know any wisdom, but when al-Khidr explained it to him, he learned the extent of its wisdom.

And so it is with us today and every day. Allah the Exalted has explained this stance by His saying: ﴿But those firmly grounded in knowledge say, "We believe in it; all is from our Lord"﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 7].

At the end of this noble verse there is what compels mankind to admit incapacity and drives them to submission, in His saying: ﴿And none knows the soldiers of your Lord except Him﴾.

Likewise, the rest of the matters from Allah, the Exalted, He is the most knowing of them. And knowledge is with Allah, the Exalted.

His saying, may He be exalted: (p-367) ﴿"What has brought you into Saqar?" They will say, "We were not of those who prayed, and we did not used to feed the poor, and we used to engage in vain discourse with those who engaged in it, and we used to deny the Day of Recompense, until there came to us the certainty.﴾

In this noble verse: the companions of the right hand question the criminals about the reason for their entry into the Fire, and the answer was that they were not among those who prayed, did not feed the needy, engaged in vain discourse with those who did so, and denied the Day of Judgment. They combined disbelief, by their denial of the Day of Judgment, with the branches of religion, which is abandoning prayer and zakah, expressed by feeding the poor and so on. This verse is therefore among the evidences that the disbeliever is held accountable for the branches of the Shari'ah along with its roots.

The Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and him, previously discussed this issue at His saying: ﴿And woe to the polytheists who do not give zakah and who, in the Hereafter, are disbelievers﴾ [Fussilat: 6–7] in Surat Fussilat.

The author said in (*Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab*):

(p-427) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah al-Muddaththir

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿Every soul is held in pledge for what it has earned﴾, the verse.

The manner of reconciling this with His words, may He be exalted: ﴿Every person is held in pledge for what he has earned﴾, the verse [al-Tur: 21], has already been explained.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 74, verse 48:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So the intercession of the interceders will not benefit them﴾

In it: that the disbelievers are not benefited by the intercession of the interceders, just as it affirms intercession for the interceders. The implication of its being that it does not benefit the disbelievers is that it benefits others.

Texts have come concerning intercession for those whom Allah approves, and texts have indicated both matters. From the texts on the absence of intercession for the disbelievers is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The wrongdoers will have no intimate friend nor any intercessor who is obeyed﴾ [Ghafir: 18].

And His saying: ﴿And none has led us astray except the criminals. So we have no intercessors﴾ [ash-Shu'ara': 99-100], and the like of that among the verses.

And in the second category is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He knows what is before them and what is behind them, and they do not intercede except for one whom He approves﴾ [al-Anbiya': 28].

Likewise, the intercessor does not intercede except for one who has been permitted to him, and they do not intercede except for those for whom they have been permitted, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 255], and His saying: ﴿On that Day, intercession will not benefit except one whom the Most Merciful has permitted and whose word He approves﴾ [Ta-Ha: 109].

The topic of intercession is broad and established in the books of creed ('aqa'id).

The summary of the matter concerning it: it does not occur except with permission from Allah for the one permitted to it. The Prophet ﷺ has been granted the Great Intercession (ash-shafa'ah al-'uzma), which is the Praiseworthy Station (al-maqam al-mahmud), and a number of intercessions after it, among them what is specific to him ﷺ, such as the Great Intercession and entry into Paradise, and intercession for a non-Muslim, namely his uncle Abu Talib, to lighten [his punishment] for him. Among them are those in which others share with him, from the prophets and the righteous. And Allah, exalted is He, knows best.

The saying of Allah, Exalted: ﴿So what is wrong with them that they turn away from the reminder?﴾ ﴿As if they were startled donkeys﴾ ﴿fleeing from a lion.﴾

In this verse there is a comparison of those who are called, in their aversion from the call and the reminder, to donkeys fleeing from hunters or from a lion. Likewise, the scholar who does not benefit from his knowledge has been compared to a donkey carrying books (asfar). These are two comparisons: one for the caller, and one for the one called when the call does not benefit him. The Shaykh (al-Shinqiti) has already discussed this in the section on enjoining good and forbidding evil (al-amr bil-ma'ruf wal-nahy 'anil-munkar).
